paragrafos: **Three measurements side by side, never added together.** Two prediction markets (Polymarket and Kalshi), voting-intention polls checked against the official notice filed with the Commission des sondages, and French press coverage. The first round is on April 18 and the runoff on May 2, 2027.

**On 11/12/2026, the two markets and the polls measure different things about Marine Le Pen.** In the win contract, Polymarket pays 46.05 and Kalshi 49.00. In polls with fieldwork up to 11/05, she is first in all 67 first-round lists of the last 45 days, from 8 pollsters, at 30.5% to 38%, and leads in the 29 runoff match-ups in which she was tested, at 52% to 70%. Her appeal to the Cour de cassation against her ineligibility is due to be ruled on by early April 2027.

**Jean-Luc Mélenchon is 2nd in the poll average and 3rd in the Polymarket win contract.** In the polls, he averages 16.9 across 50 lists from 7 pollsters over the last 30 days and places in the top two in 53 of the 67 lists of the last 45 days; in the 10 runoff match-ups in which he was tested, he trails in all of them, at 30% to 34%. In the win contract, he is at 13.50 on Polymarket and 13.00 on Kalshi.

**Two names among the top five in both markets appear in few lists of the poll database or in none.** David Lisnard is 2nd on Polymarket, at 15.75, and at 13.00 on Kalshi; in the polls, he appears in 17 of the 67 lists of the last 45 days, without placing in the top two in any of them, and averages 7.3 across 16 lists from 7 pollsters over the last 30 days. Christine Lagarde is 5th on Polymarket, at 7.25, and at 6.00 on Kalshi; no list in the database tests her. The first poll to include her, by Cluster17 for Politico, with fieldwork on 11/09 and 11/10, has been reported since 11/11, and its notice does not yet appear in the list published by the Commission des sondages. Lagarde is not a declared candidate; on 10/29, the European Central Bank announced that she will leave the bank's presidency on 02/07/2027.

**Édouard Philippe and Raphaël Glucksmann are close in the poll average and far apart in the Polymarket win contract.** Philippe averages 14.0 over the last 30 days, across 35 lists from 7 pollsters, and Glucksmann 13.6, across 47 lists from 7 pollsters; in the lists of the last 45 days in which they appear, Philippe places in the top two in 11 of 47, and Glucksmann in 3 of 56. In the win contract, Philippe is at 7.50 on Polymarket and 5.30 on Kalshi, and Glucksmann at 2.05 and 4.00.

**In the French press on 11/12, the ten headlines collected, from 8 outlets, cover six subjects.** Le Parisien and L'Opinion report the Cluster17 poll that tests Christine Lagarde. Le Monde and Le Figaro report that Jean-Luc Mélenchon's program book, "L'Avenir en commun", tops book sales, ahead of the Goncourt prize winner. Two headlines are about Bruno Le Maire: BFMTV runs his reply that there have already been many candidacies this week and there is no need to add another, and Ouest-France reports that he is preparing for the election by putting "the project before the candidate". Two are about Gabriel Attal: franceinfo reports his pledge not to cut posts in the national education system if elected, and TF1 Info announces that he is the first guest of the U2P, a small-business federation, on an LCI program. Ouest-France also reports that Bruno Retailleau proposes a primary of the right and centre on 01/31 and 02/07/2027, and Le Parisien runs Karim Bouamrane's statement that he believes in his own candidacy and in the victory of the social-democratic bloc.

**What this screen does not do.** It does not add or average the two markets, it does not turn a price into a voting intention, and it does not show a poll number without its checked official notice. On the Saturday and Sunday of each round, polls and prices are frozen, as French law of 1977 requires.
